title: Is Any Body There? Breakdown in Recovery from Traumatic Dissociation 1
abstract: Abstract The paper considers a countertransference of invisibility as pointing towards dissociative disturbance following interpersonal developmental trauma. Alongside development in many areas, the ongoing dissociative state may attract a persistent threat of breakdown accompanied by loneliness, stress and anxiety without hope of containment in the safety of another’s understanding and concern. This is understood as the loss of a ‘vertical axis’ of psychic integration with body and emotional experience, from which the ‘horizontal axis’ of capacity to feel empathically related with any body, may also collapse. For the patient to work analytically involves reconnecting to states that were dissociated during early development – an encounter with extreme pain and intolerable emotions that must be borne within the body for healing and integration to occur. The paper presents a case in which a repeating cycle of breakdowns and partial recoveries was worked through, allowing the sense of an embodied analyst—some body who had been there all along—to emerge. Three features of the analytic process are discussed: the threat of breakdown symbolised as a whirlpool circling around a deep hole; invisibility and isolation of the child’s experience as a factor in trauma; and, the internalized dark voices of critical self‐attack.
